headline: Michelle Bachelet Withdraws From Race to Become Next UN Secretary-General
seoTitle: Michelle Bachelet Withdraws From UN Chief Race | FMB News
seoDescription: Former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet withdrew from the contest to succeed António Guterres as UN secretary-general after a Security Council straw poll.
deck: The former Chilean president and UN human-rights chief ended her candidacy as the Security Council continues the process of selecting a successor to António Guterres.
author: FMB News World Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet withdrew her candidacy to become the next United Nations secretary-general. Reuters reported the withdrawal on September 20, and additional international reporting independently reported her exit from the contest.

Bachelet previously served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and twice as president of Chile. The Security Council is conducting the selection process for a successor to António Guterres, whose second term ends at the close of 2026.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Bachelet publicly ended her candidacy. Reuters reported that the decision followed a third informal Security Council straw poll in which her support declined.

sections.heading: What remains developing
paragraphs: The secretary-general selection remains open. Bachelet’s withdrawal does not determine the eventual nominee, and FMB News is not treating reported candidate standings as a prediction of the outcome.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The UN secretary-general leads the organization’s diplomatic and administrative work during a period of major conflicts, climate and development pressures, and debate over the future of multilateral institutions. The eventual selection will therefore have consequences well beyond the UN system, including for countries such as the Philippines that participate extensively in multilateral diplomacy.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Further Security Council consultations and any additional withdrawals or nominations will shape the field before the Council recommends a candidate to the General Assembly.
